event.description:
Join Liquid AI and the San Francisco AI community for an evening dedicated to decision models: purpose-built models that make fast, structured decisions without generating tokens.
Unlike language models that produce free-form text, decision models return calibrated probabilities for outcomes such as:
Noul: Should this action happen?
Choice: Which option should the system select?
Score: How should this input be rated?
Not every AI task needs generation. Routing requests, approving agent actions, moderating content, evaluating outputs and inspecting images often require a clear, reliable decision, not another paragraph of text.
Decision models offer a new way to build these systems: predictable structured outputs, calibrated confidence, low latency and zero generated tokens. They can work independently or alongside LLMs as fast decision layers for agents and production applications.
Come learn how they work, explore where they fit in the modern AI stack and see what developers are already building with Liquid's decision model family across text, vision and audio.

event.description:
89% of executives say AI increases speed, but only 6% of executives are sure they have clear examples of organization-wide AI ROI. This evening is about what's in that gap.
This after work event is for enterprise executives seeking to meet the challenge of deploying AI initiatives throughout their organization. Join the conversation and learn how your peers from Atlassian and Snowflake have transformed their workforce to embrace AI transformation.
A different kind of AI event
VentureBeat's Editor and Chief, Matt Marshall, presses leaders from Atlassian, Snowflake and WGU on what's really happening as AI reshapes their teams: where the promise matches their experience and where it doesn't. Then the floor opens to you. Come ready to share, push back and ask the hard questions. Afterward, keep the conversation going over food and drinks.
You'll leave knowing what's actually working, from the people making it work.
Thursday, Nov 12 · Doors 5:00 PM · Program 5:30 PM · Networking, food and drinks until 8:00 PM
The Agenda
Session 1: Lessons from Snowflake’s move to AI-native engineering.
Speaker: Will Allen, Head of Snowflake CoCo and CoWork, Snowflake
As agents make it faster to write code, the hard part of building a product changes. Teams still have to decide what’s worth building, check that it solves a real customer pain point, and know when it’s ready to ship. Will Allen is dealing with that shift from both sides: he builds AI products at Snowflake while also changing how his own team works with AI.
He’ll share what Snowflake has learned in its move to AI-native engineering, from spotting the early adopters who bring their teams along to rethinking engineering processes built before AI. He’ll also explain why Snowflake is leaning into early-career hiring and how AI fluency factors into hiring decisions.
Session 2: AI in Action: Building the Skills and Workflows Teams Need Now
Speaker: Dr. Molly Sands, Head of Teamwork Lab, Atlassian
Eighty-nine percent of executives say knowledge workers are moving faster with AI, but only 6% can point to a specific, measurable example of the payoff, according to Atlassian’s research. The gap isn’t effort or tools. It’s that speeding up individual tasks without rebuilding how teams actually work just creates faster collisions. This talk will trace how that disconnect shows up first in organizations, what separates the teams closing it, and how enterprises are training talent to work at the pace their AI systems now demand.
Attendees will learn:
Why faster individuals don’t mean faster organizations
What the top 14% of AI-native teams do differently
How to shift AI from a personal productivity hack to a team-level coordination layer
Session 3: The AI Skills Imperative: Individual Productivity to Enterprise Transformation.
Speaker: Paul Bingham, SVP & Executive Dean, School of Technology, WGU
AI is reshaping work at a speed the workforce has never experienced before. For 140 years, technology has transformed jobs, created new roles and made old skills obsolete. AI is following that same pattern—but on a dramatically compressed timeline. The result: a growing skills gap, widespread uncertainty, and one question on almost every employee’s mind: Will AI eliminate my job?
In this conversation, Paul Bingham explores what history can teach us about navigating technological disruption—and why the answer isn’t simply replacing workers with AI. We’ll examine how education can turn fear and hype into action by helping employees build the skills needed for jobs that are rapidly changing.
Paul will share how WGU is implementing new models, including its Applied Experience Program, designed to demonstrate what future employees can do, not just what they know. We’ll also explore how WGU’s School of Technology is building AI-forward curricula in infrastructure operations and cybersecurity based on evolving industry needs—and how employers can help trusted employees upskill before their roles are transformed.
Reserve your spot
Space is intentionally limited to keep the room small and the conversation real. This is an in-person only event.
Note: Reservations can take up to 24 hours to process. Please check your spam folder for emails from VentureBeat about the event.
event.title: Keeping Pace With AI: The Skills and Workflows Teams Need Now

event.description:
Creatives in Control: Leading with AI
AI has changed how creative teams work. Exploring is faster, iterating is cheaper, and ideas that once took weeks can be tested in an afternoon. But the questions that matter most haven’t changed: what’s right for the brand, what’s worth making, and who makes the call. That part belongs to creatives, and we think it should stay that way.
We’re bringing together design leaders from Google, Meta and Magnific who are building AI products and using AI to do it. They’ll share how their teams work day to day, where AI has made the work better, and how they keep creative direction in their hands as the tools keep changing.
On the panel
Camila Luis, Creative Strategy & AI Content Creation, Google
Michal Vaško, Product Design Lead, AI-Powered Experiences, Meta
Anthony Garcia, Marketing Leader for Leading Tech Brands
Bianka Simonidesova, Brand & Experience, Magnific
Each of them works where creativity and technology meet, in different measures. One shapes the content and stories brands tell, one designs the AI products people use every day, and one builds the brand experience around a creative platform. Together they show how creative technology has moved from a specialist corner to the center of how creative teams decide, build and lead.
The conversation will start with how AI fits into real workflows across brand, product and content, and how teams use the extra speed and volume to explore more ideas without losing what makes their work distinctive. From there, we’ll get into how creative and technical decisions are increasingly made together: who sets up the tools, who shapes the systems, and how leaders keep taste at the center as those roles blend. We’ll close with what they’d tell a team just getting started.
Who this is for
This evening is for design and creative leaders: heads of design, creative directors, brand leads, and the creative technologists building the workflows behind them. You’re probably already using AI in some way, and you’re working out how to bring it into your team in a way that makes the work better, not just faster. You might be excited, skeptical, or both. All of that belongs in the room.
Why we’re hosting it
At Magnific, we build AI tools for creatives, and we believe they should work for the people using them, not replace them. The best way we know to get that right is to listen to the leaders doing this work every day. This isn’t a product demo. It’s a space to compare notes, hear how teams at the top of the industry are adapting, and meet peers working through the same questions.

Join Swissnex in San Francisco and Irene Solaiman, Chief Policy Officer and SVP of Strategy at Hugging Face, for a conversation ahead of the Geneva AI Summit 2027.
The evening opens with a talk by Irene Solaiman, Chief Policy Officer and SVP of Strategy at Hugging Face. She’ll share her perspective on the opportunities, risks, and choices ahead as the world prepares for the AI Summit in Geneva next year.
After Irene’s talk, event attendees have the opportunity to join one of six roundtables together with the cohort of Geneva Loading… a program by Swissnex in San Francisco that brings together a group of Swiss AI experts from research, policy, business, and civil society to prepare for the Geneva AI Summit 2027.
Pick your table

What is Geneva Loading…?

Every year world leaders, tech companies, researchers, and civil society gather at a global AI Summit to decide how humanity should handle the most powerful technology of our time. Help me test-drive my first Hackaday Supercon workshop!
I'm running my first-ever workshop at Hackaday Supercon this year. It's the "exquisite corpse" drawing game, but for electronics, and I'd love to do a trial run with friendly local faces first. Come be my workshop guinea pigs!
Here's how it will work: Everyone gets a small synth module and modifies it in secret. Then we chain all the blocks together, power them up, and find out whether our collective creation plays a tune you'll recognize. Think Lego Great Ball Contraption, but for sound, with lots more ways to go gloriously wrong.
No experience needed. I'll ask for your feedback at the end, so you'll get to help shape the real thing. I will bring snacks & drinks. Come help me make it awesome?
It would mean a lot to have you there!
Workshop descriptions are online at: https://hackaday.com/2026/10/14/2026-hackaday-supercon-workshops-are-open/
My workshop description is below:
Exquisite Circuit: Exquisite Corpse for Electronics
What happens when a circuit is designed by a room full of people who cannot see the whole circuit?
In this hands-on electronic version of Exquisite Corpse, each participant adds a stage to a shared low-voltage circuit, conceals their work, and passes it to the next builder. Participants inherit standardized power and signal connections – but no schematic, explanation, or design review.
At the end, we reveal the complete creations, attempt to reconstruct their collective logic, inspect them for safety, and apply power from a strictly current-limited supply. Functionality is optional. Surprise is guaranteed.

Most robot foundation models still need your data to fine-tune, or an enterprise contract just to get access.Dream Labs took a different path. Instead of teaching robots to follow instructions, they teach them to imagine: Dream-1 predicts what the world will look like next and what the robot should do, in a single step. The team came out of NVIDIA’s GR00T group, where they helped build DreamZero, the research that put World Action Models on the map.Last month, Dream Labs came out of stealth with $90M in seed funding and launched Dream-1, a World Action Model that works zero-shot on robots it has never seen. No fine-tuning, no demos, and anyone can use it today through a public API starting at $3 an hour.
Join us for a fireside chat with You Liang, Dream Labs’ co-founder, on why imagination might be the shortcut to general robot intelligence, what it really takes to generalize across robots, and what a pay-as-you-go robot brain means for founders building in physical AI.
Topics will include:
World Action Models: How learning to predict the physical world could unlock a new paradigm for robot intelligence
The generalization problem: Moving beyond robot-specific policies toward models that work across embodiments, tasks, and environments
Scaling robot learning: The role of human video, robot data, and the training approaches that could make general-purpose robotics possible
The next frontier of Physical AI: What cheaper hardware and increasingly capable foundation models mean for robotics adoption
Building at the frontier: The research challenges, technical bottlenecks, and opportunities for founders building the next generation of Physical AI
This event is designed for founders, robotics researchers, builders, and investors actively thinking about the next generation of Physical AI.

Company Overview
InventWood turns ordinary wood into SUPERWOOD™, a breakthrough structural biomaterial that is up to 10X stronger than steel, 6X lighter, and manufacturable at half the cost of steel at scale. In addition, the material is fire rated, moisture, rot and pest resistant, and carbon sequestering. The company’s proprietary molecular re-engineering process fundamentally transforms wood by eliminating defects and increasing hydrogen bonding within the molecular structure, dramatically increasing intrinsic strength and durability.
InventWood is entering the market through premium interior and exterior building applications while building toward expansion into larger structural applications under existing mass-timber codes.
What Differentiates InventWood
Category-Defining Material — Steel-level strength at one sixth the weight, with gorgeous aesthetics and unprecedented fire resistance.
Proprietary Technology — Patented process that upgrades wood’s intrinsic performance
Commercialization Underway — SUPERMILL ONE in Frederick, MD is operational and ramping production volumes, with shipments to initial customers in market

Your AI app runs on parts you didn't build: base models, adapters, datasets, libraries. Agents pull in even more at runtime: tools, MCP servers, prompts, other agents. Each one is a way in.
In this session, we map the AI supply chain end to end: where attackers get in, and what actually stops them.
Agenda
Software vs AI supply chain: the extra steps, and why they widen the attack surface
Threat model walkthrough: data, base models, adapters, conversion and merging, model hubs, deployment
The agent's runtime supply chain: tools, MCP servers, prompt templates, other agents
Real incidents: what broke and how
Defenses and their limits: AIBOMs, signing and provenance, pinning, sandboxed loading, release gates
Open floor: your questions and your own experiences
Built on OWASP GenAI Security Project guidance. Beginners welcome, no ML background needed. No vendor pitches.

Low latency ⚡
Greater user privacy 🔒

Offline functionality 📴

event.description:
AI Cyber Alliance Meetup: Bay Area
Thursday, November 19, 2026Time: 6:00pm-8.30pmLocation: Snowflake, Silicon Valley AI Hub, 8th Floor, 135 Constitution Drive, Menlo Park, CA 94025
Join the AI Cyber Alliance at Snowflake for an evening of technical talks and conversation at the intersection of AI and cybersecurity.
Meet developers, security practitioners, researchers, founders, and others working through the opportunities and challenges of building with AI. We’ll hear from two speakers, share practical ideas, and make time to connect with the Bay Area community.
Speaker and talk details will be announced soon.
About the AI Cyber Alliance
Founded by DeepTempo, the AI Cyber Alliance is an open community advancing AI and cybersecurity through collaboration, education, and shared technical knowledge. Our meetups bring together people from industry, startups, academia, and the open source community.Speakers & Talks
Speaker 1: Josh Khalil, Implementation Consultant at Snyk.io
Talk Title: Securing how software gets built when AI agents do the building
Abstract: Coding agents like Claude Code now choose their own tools, connect to MCP servers, run commands, and install packages on developer machines. Most security teams have no visibility into any of this. Josh will run a live demo on a real machine with a few things going wrong: an MCP tool with hidden instructions, an agent trying to read secrets and run a destructive command, and generated code that pulls in a vulnerable package. He'll show how Evo by Snyk catches each before it causes damage, and what it looks like for the developer while it's happening.
Bio: Josh Khalil is an Implementation Consultant at Snyk, working with customers as they adopt AI coding agents and figure out how to keep them secure. He leads Evo onboarding for security and engineering teams, and is most interested in where agent tooling, MCP servers, and workflows meet.
Speaker 2: Dan Barahona, Founder, AISEC.university
Talk Title: AI is the New Attack Surface: Faked, Hacked and Gone Rogue
Abstract: Attackers are faking executives on video calls.  They are hijacking AI assistants through MCP servers and poisoned content.  And AI agents are deleting production data while ignoring "stop."  Dan walks through real incidents from the last year, from the $25M Arup deepfake to the first malicious MCP server to Replit's agent wiping out a database during a code freeze, and pulls out the patterns behind them.  You'll leave with a simple way to spot which AI setups are dangerous, and a short list of things to do when you get back to the office.
Bio: Dan Barahona is the founder of aisec.university and a recognized voice in the cybersecurity community. Heavily plugged into the open-source ecosystem, he focuses on providing free, accessible education and open tools to help security teams and developers defend against emerging AI vulnerabilities.
Agenda
6:00 PM – 6:30 PM: Arrival, Networking & Refreshments
6:30 PM – 7:10 PM: Talk 1: Securing how software gets built when AI agents do the building – Josh Khalil (Snyk) + Q&A

7:50 PM – 8:30 PM: Open Discussion, Networking & Wrap-upWe look forward to seeing you there!
– The AI Cyber Alliance team

What should actually become agentic?
How autonomous should an AI product be?
What changes when users specify outcomes instead of steps?
What happens when agents become a new channel to your customer?
Where does differentiation come from when everyone has access to similar AI capabilities?
How do you make product bets when the technology keeps changing?

If you’re building AI products, working on agents or deciding where AI actually belongs in your product, this is a chance to learn from someone who has built in this space and pressure-test your own thinking with a small room of product leaders and builders.

Agents are shipping code, yet humans still own the consequences. Learn from Engineering leaders across industries on what happens when agents operate in production and the stakes include real customers, sensitive data, and systems you can’t afford to break.
Join Enrich, Optimal AI and Auth0 for dinner, drinks, and a candid conversation about what it takes to put agents to work and trust its results.
We’ll dig into the decisions teams face once agents move beyond experimentation: where autonomy earns its place, where human oversight remains essential, and which pitfalls only become visible in production.
With leaders spanning fintech, robotics, security and SaaS the conversation will explore:
What breaks after deployment: Unexpected failure modes, integration challenges, and the hidden work of keeping agents reliable.
How much control to give up: Permissions, guardrails, human approvals, and knowing when to intervene.
What changes in regulated industries: Balancing speed with security, auditability, and accountability.
The new engineering playbook: How teams rethink code review, ownership, and productivity when agents become contributors.
Our Speakers:
Iba Masood, Co-founder & CEO of Optimal AI [Moderator]
Kinnar Vora, VP of AI, Forward Financing
Rebecca Yang, Director of Engineering, HubSpot
Jaehyun Yeom, Principal Software Engineer, Bear Robotics
Mitch Mikusek II, Software Engineering Manager, Verkada
After the panel, we’ll carry the conversation into dinner and mingling, with discussion prompts to help you trade production lessons, compare approaches, and unpack the challenges you’re facing with fellow engineering leaders.---------About Optimal AI:
Optimal AI is building the next frontier of quality and security for AI generated code. As code multiplies in volume by 50x, organizations are facing a multitude of new problems related to quality, review and security. Optimal is building a suite of agents (Optibots) that are thoughtful, with full codebase context and zero data retention, for this new reality of secure code review. Customers include Bear Robotics, Forward Finance, MongoDB and many more.

event.description:
Build something that could change how the world’s best skiers and snowboarders train.
Join Cloudflare and U.S. Ski & Snowboard in San Francisco on November 9 for the launch party of a new winter sports technical challenge for builders.
Cloudflare and U.S. Ski & Snowboard are teaming up to invite developers to build tools using real ski and snowboard footage/data. The goal is to explore how AI, computer vision, video analysis, and Cloudflare’s developer platform can help athletes and coaches turn competition footage into useful training insights.
At the launch party, we’ll introduce the challenge, walk through the two technical tracks, explain the available footage/data, and share how participants can build and submit projects on Cloudflare.
The Challenges - STARTER PACK
Participants can choose one challenge track or build for both. Each track includes real competition footage/data, sport-specific context, technical guidance, and example outputs to help builders understand the problem space.
Challenge 1: Snowboard Rotation Analysis 🏂
Can you teach a computer to understand a snowboard trick?
When a snowboarder launches into the air, coaches can see the trick, but measuring exactly how the rider rotates throughout the jump is much harder.
Your challenge is to build a video-analysis tool that tracks a snowboarder’s rotation during aerial tricks. Using real slopestyle and halfpipe footage, participants can identify takeoff and landing, estimate rotation angles and speed, and visualize how a rider moves through the air.
The goal is to give coaches and athletes a better way to understand what happens during a trick.
🏆 Prize: Two VIP tickets to the Toyota U.S. Grand Prix at Aspen Snowmass, February 27–28, 2027. Includes lift tickets and gift bags.
Snowboard Starter Pack: Footage, technical guidance, example outputs, and judging criteria.
Challenge 2: Alpine Race Telemetry ⛷️
Can you show exactly where a ski race was won or lost?
In Alpine skiing, races can be decided by hundredths of a second. But knowing who finished fastest does not tell coaches where an athlete gained or lost time.
Your challenge is to build a tool that turns real race footage into a live performance breakdown. Using Super-G and Downhill footage, participants can create video overlays showing estimated speed, elapsed time, and where a skier is gaining or losing time compared to another run.
Think of it as building a live analytics dashboard directly on top of ski race footage.
🏆 Prize: Two VIP tickets to the FIS Ski World Cup Finals in Sun Valley, March 20–21, 2027. Includes lift tickets and gift bags
Alpine Telemetry Starter Pack: Race footage, sample data, technical guidance, example outputs, and judging criteria.
How It Works
1. Join the launch party. Learn about the challenge, the available footage/data, the two technical tracks, and what a successful prototype could look like.
2. Pick your challenge. Choose Snowboard Rotation Analysis, Alpine Race Telemetry, or both.
3. Build and deploy on Cloudflare. Create a working prototype using whichever Cloudflare tools make sense for your project. You can use Workers, Pages, R2, Workers AI, AI Gateway, or other Cloudflare developer products.
4. Submit your project by November 30. Share your GitHub repository, a link to your deployed prototype, and a short explanation of what you built.
You do not need to be a skiing or snowboarding expert to participate. We’ve put together starter packs to help you understand the sports, the footage, and what a useful prototype could look like.
Important Dates
November 9, 5–8 PM PT: Challenge launch party in San Francisco
November 30: Project submissions due
Winners will be selected after submissions are reviewed.
The Launch Party
We’re bringing together developers, Cloudflare, and U.S. Ski & Snowboard for a launch party in San Francisco.
Attendees will learn about the challenge, the real footage/data available to builders, the athlete and coaching problems behind each track, and how to participate.
Space is limited, so please RSVP if you plan to attend.
Challenge winners will receive VIP tickets to marquee ski and snowboard events this coming winter, consolation winners will compete for a combined $80K in Cloudflare credits.

​THE EXPERIENCE
We’ll be gathering at Starlite, 21 floors within the historic Beacon Grand.
The hotel first opened in 1928, during an era when San Francisco was rapidly reinventing itself. Its Renaissance-inspired interiors were created by San Francisco architects Weeks & Day, with vaulted ceilings, gold leaf, hand-painted murals, marble, and ornate ironwork that remain part of the building today.
In the 1940s, the hotel’s private rooftop apartments were transformed into the original Starlite Room, beginning decades of rooftop gatherings, nightlife, and San Francisco stories. event.description:
Building foundation models for the physical world, whether VLAs or world models, means wrangling massive video and sensor datasets, running large-scale training and simulation, and iterating fast.
The more data these models see, the more capable they get.
Join us for an evening of technical talks and networking with fellow ML and robotics engineers and builders to see how they are tackling this new wave of physical AI innovation.
AGENDA OVERVIEW
6:00 PM - Doors open, food, and networking6:15 PM - Talks
Ury Zhilinsky, Founding Technical Member + Mouli Sivapurapu, Head of Data and App Eng, Mind Robotics
Nehil Jain, Forward Deployed Engineer, Anyscale
7:15 PM - Open networking
SESSION DETAILS
From Factory Floor to Training Run: What Works Today, What's Still Hard
Mind Robotics trains robot foundation models on egocentric video captured on live automotive production lines, plus teleop and third-party data, in a fast-growing corpus on a path to many petabytes. This talk walks through the pipeline end to end, from capture on the factory floor through QC and labeling to the training dataloader, covering what works in production today and the problems still ahead. Expect the patterns that worked and an honest list of what we haven't solved yet.
Speaker Bios:
Ury Zhilinsky leads software and AI at Mind Robotics, which makes AI-powered mobile robotic platforms for industrial manufacturing, with Rivian as its first manufacturing partner. Before Mind, his work spanned Waymo, Nuro, and Physical Intelligence.
Mouli Sivapurapu leads data and applications engineering at Mind Robotics, building the infrastructure that carries video and teleop data from the factory floor through QC and labeling into model training. Prior to Mind, he worked at Scale AI, Apple and Samsung.
Hosted by:Anyscale, the company behind the Ray open source project, is a fully managed AI platform for foundation model-scale workloads. AI teams use it to run data, training, sims, inference, and RL workloads at scale on any cloud or on-prem.
event.title: AI Infra for Physical AI: Mind Robotics x Anyscale

event.description:
AI is changing how we learn, make decisions, and navigate everyday life. How do we make the most of its possibilities while staying thoughtful about its risks?
Join The AI Collective’s Tri-Valley chapter for an evening of conversation about what AI means for us today and the future we’re helping shape.
Bringing together perspectives from technology, education, and youth advocacy, we’ll explore:
How AI is influencing human decision-making, learning, and creativity
Concerns around misinformation, privacy, overreliance, and critical thinking
How parents and schools can help students develop AI literacy and use these tools responsibly
The opportunities and challenges facing the next generation
Featured speakers
Rana Gujral is an AI entrepreneur, operator, and author of The AI Instinct (Wiley, 2026), with a foreword by Kai-Fu Lee. He is the former CEO of Behavioral Signals, an In-Q-Tel backed company building emotion and behavior AI from voice, and currently leads Renu Ventures. He serves on the board of Cartica Acquisition Corp and advises TNW and the Global AI Council. His career spans product and platform leadership at Logitech, Cricut, and Kronos. A TEDx speaker, he writes and speaks on how humans and AI will evolve together. He lives in Danville.
Amy Gao is a sophomore at Emerald High School (Dublin, CA) and the founder and president of Girls in AI, a student club dedicated to empowering girls through AI. An award-winning young innovator, Amy received the Bronze Award at AI YES 2026, third place at the Alameda County Science and Engineering Fair and more. Amy also serves as President of the Green Apple Education Foundation, which hosted 9 years of the San Ramon hackathon. A recipient of the Congressional Award Silver Medal, an AIME qualifier, and a College Board AP Scholar in freshman year, she is passionate about making AI more accessible to young people and bringing a student perspective to conversations about AI's opportunities, risks, and future impact.
Nikhil Gujral is a youth advocate, TEDx and international speaker, and youth ambassador for the AI Collective and iRAISE, where he works on AI literacy, ethical AI, and AI regulation from a next-generation perspective. He has spoken at UNESCO House in Paris and the French Consulate in San Francisco, engaging diplomats and researchers on youth voice in AI policy. A nationally ranked debater on the USA Debate Development Team, his 2025 TEDx talk, The Forgotten Joy of Hobbies, makes the case for creativity and play in a culture obsessed with output. He is a student at Monte Vista High School.
Moderator
Saba Assadi Handjani is the founder of Lumino Learning AI, a company built on a simple belief: AI should help learners stay curious and think for themselves, not do their thinking for them. A Waldorf school alum, Saba brings that tradition's focus on creativity, independent thought and the whole learner into the age of AI. Through Lumino and its AI Education Academy, an after-school program for high school students, she's preparing young people to grow alongside AI, face real challenges, and make good choices in an AI-shaped future.
Attendees
This event is open to parents, educators, community members, and anyone curious about AI’s impact. High school students are encouraged to join, and younger students are welcome with their parents. No technical background needed, just curiosity and questions.

event.description:
Is Deployment the Real Moat in Physical AI?
What does it really take to deploy robots at scale, and can deployment become a lasting competitive advantage?
As robotics foundation models and hardware continue to advance, real-world deployment remains one of the industry's biggest challenges.
What separates a successful demo from a scalable business? Is the real moat in the technology, the deployment expertise, the operational data, or the customer relationships built along the way?
Join Embodied Collective for an intimate, curated industry conversation bringing together robotics companies, deployment practitioners, and enterprise adopters to exchange firsthand insights and explore what it takes to scale Physical AI in the real world.
What We'll Explore
The Deployment Bottleneck: What's actually preventing robots from scaling beyond pilots?
The Enterprise Perspective: What do industrial buyers really need before deploying robotics solutions?
Deployment as a Moat: Can real-world experience, data, and operational capabilities create sustainable competitive advantages?
Scaling in Practice: What does it take to make robotics deployments repeatable, reliable, and commercially viable?
Confirmed Speakers
Robert Scoble | Founder, Unaligned (Opening Fireside)
Robert has spent decades on the front lines of tech, from Microsoft to eight books about the future. He now tracks AI and robotics daily at Unaligned and AlignedNews.com, and visits the teams building them, giving him a rare view of what's actually running in the real world versus what's still a demo.
Ruslan Bekbulatov | Investment Principal, Bosch Ventures
Ruslan brings a unique perspective at the intersection of industrial customers and venture investing, engaging with both sides on technology capabilities, technical specifications, deployment timelines, and commercial considerations. (Views expressed are his own and do not represent Bosch or Bosch Ventures.)
Saman Farid | Founder & CEO, Formic
Saman runs Formic, which puts robots to work in American factories, and has an active and growing fleet deployed in 150 factories. In bringing Physical AI to the real world, his team has built infrastructure and software to handle deployment, monitoring and maintenance so manufacturers can automate without large upfront costs. Before Formic, he was a Partner at Baidu Ventures, leading investments in AI companies transforming traditional industries, and he founded Robots for America to advance U.S. robotics deployment policy.
Evan Tao | Co-founder & CEO, Chestnut Robotics
Formerly a core member of Tesla's Optimus team, Evan brings extensive robotics hardware experience from Tesla, Apple, and ASML. At Chestnut Robotics, he is advancing dexterous manipulation through hardware and human demonstration co-design, focusing on making robotic systems more reliable, scalable, and deployment-ready.
Natalia Kokoromyti | Co-founder & CEO, Cybernetic Physics
A Stanford computer scientist, Natalia previously worked as a researcher in Stanford’s Scaling Intelligence Lab, where she contributed to KernelBench, and worked on confidential computing at Lucid Computing. At Cybernetic Physics, an a16z speedrun company, she is building an intelligence lab for real-world machines. The company owns the hard part of putting robots to work, from bridging sim-to-real gaps and integrating robots on-site to policy serving, teleoperation, and ongoing operations, so autonomous systems can run reliably on real floors.
Judah Longgrear | Co-Founder and President of Media, Robot.com
Judah leads Robot.com's media business, R-Ads, building a first-of-its-kind robotic media network from the company's global fleet and digital out-of-home network. Robot.com is a Physical AI platform deploying autonomous robots across delivery, logistics, advertising, and security. A serial entrepreneur, Judah has spent nearly a decade building at the intersection of mobility, adtech, and robotics.
Rajesh Senthil Kumar | Head of Product and Deployment, RLWRLD
Rajesh leads product and deployment at RLWRLD, a Physical AI company developing RLDX-1, a dexterity-first robotics foundation model designed to enable human-like manipulation. By combining real-world industrial data with advanced robot learning, RLWRLD is tackling complex manipulation tasks across manufacturing, logistics, and service environments. Rajesh brings a practical perspective on bridging foundation model capabilities with real-world deployment and commercialization.
More robotics foundation model and deployment speakers to be announced!
Who Should Join?
We're especially looking to connect with:
Robotics Deployment Companies: Founders and operators building and deploying robotics solutions in real-world environments.
Enterprise Buyers & Adopters: Manufacturing, logistics, industrial, and other organizations actively deploying, piloting, or evaluating robotics technologies.
System Integrators & Deployment Partners: Teams working directly on robotics integration, implementation, and operations.
Our goal is to bring the people building and deploying robotics together with the businesses adopting them — creating a focused, high-signal conversation around real challenges, practical insights, and potential collaborations.

event.description:
Did Jesus Christ actually rise from the dead?
To most of us in the modern world, the question is almost so ridiculous that it's not even worth asking. Sure, Jesus may have had a few insightful moral teachings. It may even be the case that some find comfort and guidance from faith in Jesus. But to say that a 33 year old man from the backwaters of Galilee in the first century AD literally died, was buried, and miraculously came back to life is, at the very least, a bit ridiculous.
In this talk, Aditya Prathap will be making the case for why the resurrection of Jesus Christ is not only not ridiculous, but is in fact the only rational explanation of the objective historical data.
The talk will cover what is known as the Minimal Facts Argument. Concepts and sources that will be discussed include but are not limited to the following:
What Tacitus' comments on Christ in Annals (116 AD) tells us about the crucifixion of Christ.
What records of early Christian persecution from Suetonius (112 AD) and Pliny the Younger (121 AD) and the creed cited by the Apostle Paul in his letter to the Corinthians (54 AD) reveal about the sociopolitical landscape surrounding early Christians and its corresponding incentive structure.
Analysis of the medical literature relevant to common natural explanations of the historical data, including grief-induced hallucinations, mass hallucinations, and the symptoms of asphyxiation, the primary mechanism of death in Roman crucifixion.
Scholarly frameworks used to identify the reliability of data, e.g., the criterion of embarrassment.
People of any religious background or lack thereof are welcome to join. Skepticism and pushback are encouraged. No background in history or theology is needed. The talk will last ~45 minutes, followed by Q&A.
Aditya is a Christian living in San Francisco. Raised Hindu, he became an atheist after growing disillusioned with organized religion. After over a year of investigating the historical evidence for Christianity to prove that it had no rational justification, Aditya became convinced of the historicity of the resurrection of Jesus and was baptized in 2019.
event.title: The Historical Case for the Resurrection of Christ

This House welcomes AI agents shopping on behalf of humans.
AI agents can already compare prices, fill carts and check out without you. This year, Amazon went to court to keep them out of its store. So who's right?
Two founders take opposite sides in a live, Oxford-style debate. You vote before it starts and again at the end.
The debaters
For the motion: John Lunsford, founder of Tethral AI. He's building a headless AI shopper that plugs into your favorite AI assistant and buys within limits you set.
Against the motion: Magesh Vadivelu, former Amazon seller. He built and sold his own fabric brand on Amazon, and knows firsthand how thin seller margins are. His question: when an AI agent shops wrong, who pays for the return?
I've tried it myself. I let a Grok bot order my lunch on Uber Eats, and it worked. I'm still arguing against. Coming in person or not, watch what happened before you pick a side:
The format
Opening statements: 3 minutes each
Two rounds of rebuttals: 3 minutes each
Closing statements: 3 minutes each
Final audience vote
There are no interruptions and no open Q&A. Just two founders, one motion and a room that decides.

This latest volume features twenty-one brand-new, groundbreaking, gruesome tales—authored by both established (Tommy Orange! Stephen Graham Jones!) and newly unearthed Indigenous talent. event.description:
For Ten Lives, her first book, Pulitzer Prize-winning data journalist Mona Chalabi followed ten people with ten different incomes, all of them afraid for their futures. She documents how wealth shaped their feelings, their choices, their identities, and their insecurities. For five years, she researched the data behind their taxes, groceries, and inheritances to understand the systems that keep people stuck.
But then, she too found herself facing the same fears, when her mother’s sudden illness and subsequent medical bills threatened her own financial safety and made the questions she had been writing about all too real. How much money is enough? To live a “good” life? To protect the people you love in an emergency?Interweaving her own story with those of her interviewees and illustrated throughout with the data visualizations for which Chalabi is renowned, Ten Lives asks how much wealth it takes to be safe in the United States.
She'll be joined in conversation by writer Rahawa Haile. Her book, In Open Country, is forthcoming from Little, Brown. It is a blended memoir about her thru-hike of the Appalachian Trail and the politics of free movement in the US.

Abstract:
Modern machines are made of many memories: host DRAM, GPU HBM, shared memory, and the links between devices. Even modern compilers do not know about them, so a pointer to the wrong device shows up only at runtime(resulting in data corruption or segfault).
Vx, a new systems language, tracks where the object lives and where this runs as compile-time facts.
I'll talk about the language facilities that enable programmers to express provenance. Moreover, I'll talk about how function contracts (requires and ensures) proves that tensor indices stay in bounds and rejects a program with incorrect stride.
I'll share the bugs Vx catches before anything runs and show where an SMT solver fits in a production compiler and where it stops.
Speaker: Aditya Kumar (https://x.com/adityazero_)
Vx: https://vxlang.org/

event.description:
Join us Tuesday, November 3rd at 5:30 PM for an evening with Stefanie Hutka, design leader and author of What Your Machines Should Do: The Science and Strategy of Human-Centered Automation. Stefanie has spent her career asking a question that sounds simple until you try to answer it: what should automation actually do, and for whom?
Her talk centers on what she calls the "Automation Strategy Gap," the yawning distance between an organization's AI ambitions and its actual readiness to do something useful with them. It is, she argues, alarmingly wide. Drawing on human factors, cognitive science, and management theory, her book makes the case that AI is the latest chapter in a long history of automation, and that the durable lessons were always there, we just got distracted by the hype. One particularly useful provocation: automation accelerates the system you already have. Which means the first thing worth mapping is the beliefs driving your organization before you automate anything at all.
This is a book launch talk. It will be an essential conversation for anyone who has sat through a roadmap presentation where "AI-powered" was doing a lot of heavy lifting where a strategy should have been.This event is free and open to the public.....................​Design Field Notes is a lecture series where we invite the public to the UC Berkeley campus for conversations with designers, makers and artists who are contributing to shaping the future through design.If you require accommodation for a disability for effective communication (ASL interpreting/CART captioning, alternative media formats, etc.) or information about campus mobility access features in order to fully participate in this event, please contact Jacobs Institute staff at jacobsinstitute@berkeley.edu with as much advance notice as possible and at least 7-10 days in advance of the event.

Inspired by the VFX collective Corridor Crew’s video “Can modern VFX Artists use 90’s software?”, we’re hosting a Bryce 3D Live event here in San Francisco.
10 artists with different practices will be making live worlds and scenes with Bryce 7.1 on a collection of 15-year-old working iMac G5s donated to TIAT from the Internet Archive. There will also be a version available in an online emulator for you to try it yourself on your own laptop. + We’ll have a surprise panel to vote on the coolest images.
Bryce (named after Bryce Canyon, Utah) is 3D modeling software first released by MetaTools in 1994 released until 2010. If you’ve ever seen Trapper-Keeper-core graphics of floating islands with mirrored spheres, some rusty pipes with tendrils in a devastated world (but there's also a chess piece), or a glowing orb on a cover of an ambient music CD from 2002 you found in a thrift store, that was probably made with Bryce!
Its skeuomorphic interface (designed by Kai Krause) has alien-like buttons and is confusing as hell to play with, but that’s why it’s fun. During the peak of digital art webrings from 1998-2002 hobbyists across the world built scenes and shared them in online galleries. (And people are still doing this today on r/Bryce3D!) I’ll kick off the event with some Bryce / Metascape lore and images I dug up on the Wayback machine.
Event Schedule
2:00-2:15pm - Mingle time + artists gather around the computers
2:15pm - Intro to the Strangeness of Metascape and early Bryce Communities (a short talk)
2:30pm - Artists begin 3D modeling! You can observe them, hang out, or play with Bryce too
4:30pm - Judgement Ceremony with special guest panelists
5:00pm - Say goodbye
Artists:Jordan Metz (@jor__art)Shubha Jagannatha (@shubhastudios)Jason Eppink (@jasoneppink)Caroline Hermans (@caromakercomics)Enchax (@chaxnsee)Isaac Gierard (@igierard) + more TBA
Emulator and streaming by Britt Selvitelle + InfiniteMac with software from Macintosh Repository
Artifacts from Susan A. Kitchens (author of Real World Bryce 4) and special guest Phil Clevenger (UX design director of KPT Bryce 1.0 & Bryce 2).
Hosted by Danielle Baskin (@djbaskin)
Bring a laptop if you want to play too! But you are very welcome to hang out and watch.

Small Batch Meetup is a small Data + AI meetup for people who live or work in the Tri-Valley. Join us at Inklings Coffee & Tea in downtown Pleasanton on Sunday, Nov 15 for a relaxed afternoon: one deep dive on real work, lightning talks, and good conversation. Every experience level is welcome.
Just 10 seats, and it's free. This batch is full, so join the waitlist, or join on Luma at luma.com/smallbatchmeetup to hear about new dates!
📍 Inklings Coffee & Tea, 530 Main St, Pleasanton (the Riddermark room)🗓️ Sun, Nov 15, 3 PM - 5 PM🍪 Snacks thanks to our sponsor, Zenphi (drinks at the counter)💬 Join our Discord to meet the group before Sunday: smallbatchmeetup.com/discord
Before You RSVP
Please RSVP only if you plan to come, so every seat gets used. Plans changed? Cancel on Luma so someone on the waitlist gets your seat.
Featured Speaker
From POC to production: my experience standing up a data platform
The company I work for grew through acquisitions, so its data sits in lots of separate systems. Instead of copying everything into one warehouse, my team uses one SQL engine, Dremio, to query about 40 sources directly. The proof of concept (POC) ran on one VM in March 2024, and reaching production took about 18 months. I'll talk about running the platform on Kubernetes and the other teams it depends on. I'll also cover what comes after production, and what running my own agents at home taught me about that next step.
Give a Talk
Lightning talks happen on the spot: anyone can take five minutes to share something cool they've been working on or something they want to talk about. No prep needed! Want to give a deep dive at a future meetup? Just let us know: share your idea at smallbatchmeetup.com/talk, or use Contact the Host. We love practical, vendor-neutral Data + AI talks about real work, at every level.
Agenda
Getting There
Inside Inklings Coffee & Tea
Where: we meet in the Riddermark room inside Inklings Coffee & Tea, 530 Main St, downtown Pleasanton. Grab your own drink at the counter on the way in, then head to the back of the cafe, to the large room with the stage and open seating. Look for the Small Batch sign in front of a room, and that's us!
Parking: Park in the Inklings Coffee & Tea lot (driveway off Main St, just north of the building). Full? Try the public lot off W Neal St (enter from W Neal St or W Angela St, 4 min walk) or the public lot off Peters Ave (4 min walk).
Access: questions about access? Ask through Contact the Host, and we'll check with Inklings Coffee & Tea before the day.
Sponsors
Zenphi · snacks
Zenphi helps organizations put AI to work inside real business processes, reliably, securely and at scale: AI agents, workflow automation, human approvals and integrations, built for Google Workspace and beyond. Through its Community Sponsorship, Zenphi is covering the snacks at this batch. Thank you, Zenphi.
🖥️ More at zenphi.com📲 Follow Zenphi on LinkedIn
FAQ
Can I come if I don't live in the Tri-Valley?
Yes. Small Batch Meetup is meant for people who live or work in the Tri-Valley, and anyone and everyone is invited. With 10 seats, when a batch is full, we may remove an RSVP from someone who doesn't live or work in the Tri-Valley to make room for someone who does.
What if a batch is full?
Join the waitlist. When someone cancels, we give their seat to someone on the waitlist, and Luma emails you if it's yours.
Do I have to give a talk or introduce myself?
Only if you want to. Lightning talks happen on the spot, and the first half hour is just time to grab a drink and meet people. Coming on your own? We'll introduce you around. Every experience level is welcome, from students and career changers to seasoned engineers.
Can I get the slides afterward?
Yes. After each batch, the deep dive's recording goes on the home page when the speaker agrees, and the slides and photos go up in the Discord: smallbatchmeetup.com/discord
Can I bring a friend?
Yes, please share the event with them. Have them save their own seat on Luma, since there are only 10. If it's full, they can join the waitlist.

event.description:
Happily Ever After?｜从此，幸福地生活下去?
Future of Family in the Age of AI｜AI 时代的家庭未来
童话故事总以“从此幸福地生活在一起”结束，而真实的生活，或许需要我们不断学习这句话的意义。
当 AI 改变学习、工作，以及我们对未来的想象，我们该如何为自己，也为所爱的人，创造幸福的生活？
今年的 Future of Family Forum，邀请你用一天的时间，从三种熟悉的情绪出发，一起聊聊家庭与人生：
焦虑｜与不确定的未来相处当熟悉的教育与职业道路不再确定，我们和孩子真正需要的是什么？
愤怒｜在冲突中重新靠近伴侣之间的争吵背后，有哪些需要渴望被听见？我们如何理解彼此，修复关系？
爱｜重新理解父母，也理解自己长大之后，我们如何重新看待自己的父母？又希望把怎样的爱，传递给下一代？
这里有真实的故事、坦诚的对话，也有留给自己思考与感受的空间。你不需要带着答案而来，带着好奇、困惑，以及真实的自己，就很好。
2026 年 11 月 21 日，周六｜上午 9:00 开始｜美国太平洋时间｜全天活动
门票包含全天活动、午餐，以及从上午至下午晚些时候供应的茶点与饮品。
也许，“从此幸福地生活下去”不是故事的结局，而是我们一起学习的能力。
Fairy tales end with “happily ever after.” Real life asks us to keep learning what that means.
As AI reshapes how we learn, work, and imagine the future, how do we build a good life—for ourselves and the people we love?
Join us for a day of honest conversations around three emotions:
Anxiety: When familiar paths through education and work become uncertain, what do we—and our children—really need?
Anger: Behind everyday conflicts with our partners, what needs are asking to be heard? How can we find our way back to each other?
Love: As we grow older, how do we understand our own parents differently—and choose what we pass on to the next generation?
Through shared stories, thoughtful conversations, and time to reflect, we’ll explore these questions together. You don’t need to have the answers. Come with your curiosity, your questions, and yourself.
November 21, 2026 · 9:00 AM Pacific · A full day together
Your ticket includes full-day admission, lunch, and refreshments from morning through late afternoon.
Perhaps “happily ever after” isn’t an ending, but something we learn to practice

event.description:
Computational Poetry: Tools for Playing with Language
Workshop led by Alicia Guo
This workshop will introduce participants to computational poetry, an act of treating language as a poetic material that can be examined, shaped, and animated through computation. We’ll explore the history of computational poetry and processes through artists and writers who have used rules, algorithms, and code as core methods of their work. Together, we’ll recreate a few computational poetry works and use them as a pathway to learn tools for working with language in code, including RiTa and Nounsing.
Participants will then adapt, combine, or break these techniques to create a computational poem of their own, taking on the form of an endlessly generating poem, a text that changes over time, a strange language machine, or something else entirely.
Workshop Prerequisites:
Laptops required
No coding experience necessary, though those who are more comfortable with code will have options to dive deeper
About the Instructor:
Alicia Guo is a computational poet, artist, and human-computer interaction researcher working to reimagine and redesign our relationships with creative technology. She is currently pursuing a PhD at the University of Washington, working in creativity support tools and theory.
Across websites, performances, writing systems, physical installations, and participatory experiments, she is interested in technologies that are alive to process: things that change, decay, invite response, or reveal the traces of how they were made. She creates poetic instruments that invite participation: artifacts that create artifacts that create artifacts. Her research is rooted in her art and writing practice, and often begins from questions of who gets to shape a system? What kinds of creative labor become visible or invisible? How do tools change what we notice? Her computational poetry has appeared in magazines such as The HTML Review, Michigan Quarterly Review, Taper, Ensemble Park, and Graywolf Lab. Her installations have been shown in spaces including Gray Area, Vector Festival, and Voidspace.
You can find some of her work on her website or on Instagram.
This Workshop is part of our new Patch Bay series:
A weekly series of workshops, demos, and talks for media artists creative technologists in the Bay Area
​Wednesdays, 6 PM
Patch Bay is a new weekly series for anyone in the Bay Area who wants to get hands-on with emerging technology, grapple with the big questions AI is raising in creative fields, and connect with the wider world of media arts, design, and engineering. It's a space to plug in for newcomers who want to get involved at Gray Area for the first time, and for longtime members of our community ready to share new, experimental work.
We keep the format flexible from week to week, so there's room to experiment, talk, and learn. You might catch a workshop on building poetic tools for the web, a round of lightning talks on agentic AI experiments, an artist talk on immersive installations, or a live-coded audiovisual performance that turns code into sound and image in real time. No two weeks look the same.
All Patch Bay events are sliding scale, NOTAFLOF.
Got an idea for a future session?Email learn@grayarea.org and tell us about it.We especially want to hear from people who've been looking for a way to share their bold, critical, and creative work at Gray Area but weren't sure where to get started.
Event Logistics:
Workshops and talks are open to all ages. Children under the age of 16 should be supervised by a parent.
Workshop attendees should bring their own laptops.
Workshops will take place in the classroom and are not ADA accessible.
Talks will be seated in the theater.

Beyond the Demo: Building and Funding Physical AIAutonomy · Real-World Deployment · Commercialization · Venture Capital
Presented by House of 434

About the Event
A Physical AI system that works in a demo is impressive. Building one that works reliably in the real world is an entirely different challenge.
As AI moves beyond screens into machines, factories, vehicles, laboratories, and other physical environments, a new generation of founders is building intelligent systems that can perceive, learn, decide, and act.
But turning these breakthroughs into successful companies comes with unique challenges. How do founders build defensible technology? What does it take to move from research and prototypes into real-world deployments? And what makes a Physical AI company attractive to investors?
Following our Founder × Funder gatherings in New York City, we’re bringing the series to San Francisco.
Physical AI Founder × Funder brings together technical founders, active investors, robotics researchers, and industry leaders for an evening exploring the opportunities and challenges of building and funding Physical AI companies.
Expect a candid founder-investor panel, five selected startup pitches, and dedicated time for meaningful introductions between people building and backing the next generation of Physical AI.
Physical AI Founder × Funder brings together technical founders, active investors, researchers, and industry leaders for an evening focused on the technologies and companies shaping the future of Physical AI.
After our New York editions, we're bringing the series to San Francisco.______________________________________________________________
What We're Exploring
World Models & Physical Simulation
AI systems that learn how physical environments behave, predict future states, and simulate outcomes. From learned world models and digital twins to physics-based AI and sim-to-real transfer.
Perception & Physical Data
Autonomy & Embodied Intelligence
How do machines learn to perceive, reason, and act in complex physical environments? From robot learning and intelligent control to autonomous planning and adaptive systems.
From Simulation to Real-World Deployment
What does it take to move beyond controlled demonstrations and build intelligent systems that operate reliably in unpredictable environments?
Perception, Physical Data & Continuous Learning
How proprietary physical data, sensor fusion, perception systems, and real-world feedback loops improve autonomous systems and create defensible advantages.
Physical AI Infrastructure
The software and infrastructure required to train, evaluate, deploy, monitor, and improve Physical AI systems, including edge intelligence, reliability, and execution platforms.
Commercialization & Venture Capital
What does it take to turn a technical breakthrough into a venture-scale business? We’ll explore customer adoption, pilot programs, deployment economics, technical differentiation, and what investors look for at the earliest stages.______________________________________________________________
Who Should Attend?
Founders Building Physical AI
We’re particularly interested in technical founders building:
Autonomous systems and embodied intelligence
Robotics software and intelligent control
Perception, spatial intelligence, and sensor fusion
Physical data infrastructure and continuous learning
Simulation-to-real-world technologies
Edge intelligence and real-time autonomy
Robotics deployment, evaluation, and reliability infrastructure
Industrial autonomy and intelligent automation
Enabling software and infrastructure for Physical AI
Whether you’re coming out of a research lab, developing a prototype, running early pilots, or preparing to raise capital, we’d love to learn what you’re building.
We’re especially interested in pre-seed and seed-stage founders with deep technical expertise, differentiated technology, and a clear vision for commercial applications.
Investors & Funders
We’re inviting active angels, venture capital firms, specialist Physical AI investors, deep-tech funds, corporate venture teams, and family offices interested in backing technical founders.
Particularly relevant are investors focused on robotics, embodied intelligence, autonomous systems, AI infrastructure, industrial technology, and frontier technologies.
Researchers & Industry Leaders
We also welcome select robotics researchers, AI engineers, technical executives, and industry operators working across autonomous systems, manufacturing, logistics, agriculture, industrial technology, and physical infrastructure.
______________________________________________________________The Founder × Funder Panel
Beyond the Demo: Building and Funding Physical AI
What separates an impressive technology demonstration from an intelligent system that can operate reliably in the real world, and a company investors want to back?
We’re bringing together experienced founders, technical leaders, and investors for a candid discussion about the journey from breakthrough technology to commercial deployment and venture investment.
We’ll explore:
Where are the biggest opportunities in Physical AI beyond the hype?
What are the hardest challenges in moving autonomous systems from research to real-world deployment?
What creates lasting defensibility: proprietary data, intelligent models, software infrastructure, or deployment experience?
Should founders build full-stack robotics businesses or focus on the intelligence and infrastructure layers?
What technical and commercial milestones make a Physical AI startup fundable at pre-seed and seed?
Where would experienced founders and investors place their bets today?

Swissnex in San Francisco regularly hosts Connect Lunches to strengthen connections and collaboration between Swissnex in San Francisco and the Bay Area academia ecosystem. This Connect Lunch is part of Geneva Loading…, a program by Swissnex in San Francisco and Mercator Foundation Switzerland that prepares eleven Swiss-based AI experts from academia, civil society, media, policy and industry to contribute to the AI Summit 2027 in Geneva (June 21–22, 2027).
From November 16–20, 2026, the cohort spends a week in the Bay Area, inside the ecosystem where frontier AI is built, funded and contested. About Trigger.dev
Trigger.dev is the open-source, developer-first platform for building, running and scaling reliable AI agents, background tasks and event-driven workflows in TypeScript and Python. It's backed by Y Combinator (W23), has 16.8k+ stars on GitHub, and powers billions of runs at companies like Cal.com, MagicSchool AI and Midday.
Just launched: chat agent
Durable AI chat that runs on a machine with no timeouts and keeps streaming through refreshes and crashes. The machine sleeps when nobody's typing and wakes where it left off, with no state for you to manage.
No timeout on a turn. In production, 1 run in 20 lasts longer than 36 minutes.
Durable streams. Refresh mid-response and it replays from where you stopped reading.
Waiting is free. An agent can pause for a human approval all weekend without running up a bill.
Tracing built in. Cost, tokens and latency per model, with nothing to instrument.
Come ask Matt, James, Daniel, and Eric how it works, and what they're seeing as teams take agents to production.

Equator started in 1995 in a Marin garage, and 30 years later, they are one of the Bay Area's most respected roasters.
California's first B Corp coffee roaster and an early adopter of Fair Trade in 1999 and helping pioneer direct trade.

Join us in Grace Cathedral as we read excerpts from Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on humanity in the age of artificial intelligence, Magnifica Humanitas. Quoting the likes of Dorothy Day, Maria Montessori, Martin Luther King, Jr., and J.R.R. Tolkien, the encyclical asks should we use AI to build a new Tower of Babel or choose to “build a city in which God and humanity dwell together?” More than a treatise on technology, the encyclical touches on the foundations of social justice, namely, the inherent dignity of humanity, the importance of labor, the meaning of relationships, and our “pressing duty to remain profoundly human.”
The reading will be “in the round” with attendees taking turns reading a paragraph. After the reading, we will convene for refreshments and further conversation. Please join us.

event.description:
Frontier Paper Club — Palo Alto
Papers. People. Possibilities.
How do we know an AI agent is actually getting better? What makes a research result hold up beyond its benchmark? And which ideas are ready to become systems people can depend on?
Frontier Paper Club is a monthly gathering in Palo Alto for researchers, engineers, and founders exploring the next generation of AI. Sponsored by Startup Island Taiwan and Blobfish.ai, we bring together people developing new methods, building agent systems, and testing what works in practice.
Each session centers on 2–3 papers, benchmarks, or technical implementations selected around a shared research question. Topics span AI agents, reinforcement learning, post-training, reasoning, memory, evaluation, and simulation environments.
Presentations are brief and technically grounded, leaving plenty of time to examine the work together: the assumptions behind a method, the strength of its evidence, the details needed to reproduce it, and the failures that suggest where research should go next.
​🕒 Evening format
5:30pm Arrivals & IntroductionsMeet fellow researchers and builders. Share what you’re working on and the questions you’re hoping to explore.
6:00pm Research Presentations & Benchmark DiscussionPresenters walk through the problem, approach, key results, and limitations. Each talk is followed by audience questions and technical discussion.
7:30pm Open Conversation & NetworkingContinue the discussion, exchange implementation notes, and meet potential collaborators.
Qizheng Zhang: Can AI agents make meaningful contributions to frontier computer science research?
FrontierCS 2 introduces 48 open-ended research tasks across 13 domains, from machine learning systems and high-performance computing to databases and robotics. Each task starts from a published paper and its code, removes the key contribution, and challenges agents to rediscover it through iterative experimentation in a real research environment. We evaluate 12 frontier agents, with the strongest achieving a 58% pass rate, while 16 tasks remain unsolved by any agent.
FrontierCS 2 - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.29932
Dhanashree Lele: Can AI agents improve through their own experience?
Dhanashree Lele will present a critical analysis of Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems by Erkang Zhu and colleagues at Alibaba Research (2026). The talk will examine how Recursa uses collaborating agents to refine instructions, skills, and memory while keeping the underlying models fixed, exploring the authors’ reported results, methodological limitations, and implications for adaptive AI systems.
"Zhu et al. (2026), arXiv:2611.04035v1 - https://arxiv.org/html/2611.04035v1
​📝 Want to present your work?
Have research or an implementation you’d like to discuss with Bay Area’s AI community?
We’re accepting submissions covering:
AI agents, reasoning, planning, and memory
Reinforcement learning and post-training
Benchmarks, evaluation methods, and agent reliability
Simulation environments and synthetic training data
Reproductions, negative results, and practical lessons from deployment
Share a link to your paper, benchmark, project, or slides, along with what you’d like to present. Submissions will be considered for upcoming sessions.
Submit your work here →
Questions? Contact johnny@blobfish.ai.
​🤝 Sponsored by
Startup Island TAIWAN - Silicon Valley Hub
Startup Island TAIWAN is a national initiative supporting Taiwanese startups expanding globally. Located in Palo Alto, the Silicon Valley Hub connects founders with investors, corporate partners, and innovation ecosystems while serving as a bridge between Taiwan and Silicon Valley.
The Hub regularly hosts events, delegation visits, founder programs, and ecosystem gatherings that strengthen collaboration between Taiwan's technology ecosystem and the global innovation community.
Blobfish.ai
Blobfish.ai builds training gyms for AI agents—simulated enterprise environments where models practice workflows across tools such as CRMs, ERPs, and spreadsheets.
Its environments combine realistic data, executable tools, adjustable task difficulty, and deterministic checks of task outcomes. As models improve, Blobfish generates new challenges to support continued learning, with a focus on the complex, multi-step work agents need to perform in practice.

Experience an authentic Japanese tea ceremony in a welcoming, hands-on workshop led by a Japanese tea ceremony instructor.
Harue Imaizumi practices and teaches the Omotesenke way of tea in Berkeley. She has studied tea in both Japan and the United States and is a certified instructor of the Omotesenke school. Through her practice and teaching, she is dedicated to sharing wa no kokoro—the spirit of harmony.
During the workshop, guests will learn about Japanese tea culture, matcha culture, and the wellness benefits of matcha, while being introduced to a table-style Japanese tea ceremony.
You’ll learn the basic principles and etiquette of Japanese tea ceremony, as well as practical tips for preparing delicious matcha at home—including matcha-to-water ratio, water temperature, and whisking techniques. You’ll then whisk your own bowl of matcha and enjoy it with traditional Japanese sweets.
The tea will come from ochamode, founded by Mayuka Inaba. Originally from Kikugawa, a tea-growing town in Shizuoka, Japan, Mayuka grew up with ocha as part of everyday life. She founded ochamode in Berkeley in 2021. Through high-quality organic matcha and green teas grown by farmers in her home region of Shizuoka, she shares the Japanese ocha lifestyle that nurtures well-being in both body and mind.
Program
Introduction to matcha, Japanese tea culture, and the story behind ochamode
Learn about the traditions, principles, and etiquette of Japanese tea ceremony
Experience a table-style Japanese tea ceremony demonstration
Learn about matcha and its wellness benefits
Hands-on guidance on how to whisk your own bowl of matcha
Enjoy freshly prepared matcha with traditional Japanese sweets
Practical tips for making delicious matcha at home, including matcha-to-water ratio, water temperature, whisking techniques, preventing clumps, storage, and matcha latte preparation
Q&A with the tea ceremony instructor and ochamode founder
Ticket Options
Basic Ticket — $60
Includes:
Full 75-minute workshop experience
30g tin of ochamode Organic Okumidori Matcha from Shizuoka, Japan ($32 value)
Matcha served during the workshop
Traditional Japanese sweets
Matcha Bowl Ticket — $85
Includes everything in the Basic Ticket, plus:
One Japanese-made matcha bowl to take home
Members get $10 off. Just pick the the member ticket!

On November 21 at 10:00 am, NODE will join a cohort of museums and institutions around the world for a live broadcast of Act III, the third and final act of Human Unreadable (2023-2026) by Operator, performed at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York. We invite you to experience the work together, in a shared space, in real time.
Since its conception in 2022, ACT III has found new ways to ask how much of a body survives its translation into code, and its conceptual arc has always been the slow recovery of the human.
Merging choreography and code, ACT III relies on a library of dance movements and a generative choreography method stored on the Ethereum blockchain. Act III is an 80-minute multimedia performance using dance sequences #2–101 from the Human Unreadable collection as the raw choreographic material, woven together through scripted dialogue, lighting and scenic design, performance art, and set to an original score.
The broadcast is conceived as an artwork in its own right, with footage edited and altered in real time as the performance unfolds.Doors open at 9:30. Please arrive early. Seating will be limited.

It’s 2050, and San Francisco is thriving. Our energy is abundant, reliable, and clean. Our green spaces are protected. Writers, activists, and working class San Franciscans are filling thousands of new homes with music and joy. Bicycles, pedestrians and electric buses and trains fill our streets. Aina is an AI wearable that knows what you need, a new way to control your apps, agents and devices, beyond phone touchscreens and keyboards.For the past 15 months, we've been building in stealth as a Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) lab, working closely with a small group of early adopters to answer two questions:
What comes after the touchscreen?
What is the right hardware interface for the age of AI?
We've spent that time obsessing over how AI will change the way we use computers over the next 5 to 10 years, and how we can make interacting with it feel more natural and effortless.
After building 100s of prototypes, exploring multiple form factors, shipping experimental interfaces for research like Dune(a context aware keypad for mac which got pretty popular earlier this year), and running a private pilot of our flagship interface Aina, we're finally ready to show you what we've built.
For the first time, we'll unveil the hardware, demonstrate everything it can do, and take you through the journey from our earliest experiments to the finished product.

event.description:
A hands-on workshop: leave with a ranked list of use cases for your solution and a plan to test them with the customers, users, and stakeholders who matter.
Most technology solutions can be applied in more than one way. Each use case brings different customers, different users, and different stakeholders, and choosing which one to pursue first shapes your go-to-market, your pilots, your roadmap, and your next raise. A structured look makes that choice easier than gut feel alone.
This is a working session, not a talk. You’ll apply a market hypothesis framework, delivered as a Claude skill, to your own solution, on your own or in a small team. The skill gives you a first pass: possible use cases, the people involved in each, and a score on the same criteria. Then we focus on what a score can’t tell you, which is what to ask real people and how to test your assumptions through conversations.
How the session works:
Describe your solution and the use cases you have in mind (or let the skill suggest some)
Map who is involved in each use case: customers who buy, users who work with it, and stakeholders who influence or approve it
Score and compare use cases on pain, budget, speed of decision, and scale
Ask the scale question: choose a first use case that delivers a near-term win and still points toward where you want to be long term
Turn your top use cases into assumptions you can test
Draft your validation plan: who to talk to across all three groups, what to ask, and how to run the calls
Share out, with a few volunteers getting live feedback
Who this is for: Founders and teams building technology solutions at any stage, from seed to series A. Hardware, software, AI-enabled products,  are all welcome.
Bring: a laptop with a Claude account, a short description of your solution, and teammates if you’d like to work as a team. Bring your own lunch.

event.description:
Join the Snorkel AI Reading Group, a recurring forum to explore the latest frontier developments in AI while building meaningful connections within the community.
As AI workloads grow, data center infrastructure is strained by rising energy and capacity demands. Yet many queries are everyday tasks (drafting, summarizing, looking things up) that may not need frontier-scale models running in the cloud. Knowing how to measure efficiency brings us closer to building AI that is within everyone’s reach without outgrowing the power we have to run it.
In this session, Stanford researchers Jon Saad-Falcon and Avanika Narayan will present their work on Intelligence per Watt (IPW): Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI, where IPW serves as a unified metric to measure intelligence efficiency by capturing capabilities delivered against power required.
Among other things, you'll learn:
How measuring intelligence per watt gives researchers, builders, and policymakers a common yardstick for deciding where AI should run as demand outpaces power supply
How efficiency measurements across models and hardware can show which queries belong where
Why weighting capability against real-world economic tasks reveals where AI creates value, and where gaps remain
Across 20+ models and 8 accelerators, tested on 1M real-world queries, how local AI efficiency has changed over time
Agenda:4 pm - doors open4:30 pm - talk begins5:30 pm - research discussion and networking
🧋🧋🧋 Boba tea and other refreshments will be provided ! 🧋🧋🧋
This work has been featured in the Financial Times, Reuters, and Foreign Affairs, and was recently accepted to NeurIPS 2026. arXiv preprint available here.
The broader research has also been featured through interviews, talks, and industry coverage from Foundation Capital, AMD’s Advancing AI conference, PyTorch Conference’s Measuring Intelligence Summit, IBM Research, and SambaNova.
Jon Saad-Falcon and Avanika Narayan are PhD students in Computer Science at Stanford University and members of Hazy Research.
event.title: Reading Group (+🧋): How Efficiently does AI Turn Energy into Useful Work?

Read:1. The Medium is the Metaphor (pgs 3-15)2. Media as Epistemology (pgs 16-29)3. Typographic America (pgs 30-43)Next week we will read the rest of Part 1. --WHAT IS THIS?this is a reading and discussion circle, focused on media theory, spectacle, and the politics, sociology, and anthropology of technology through an STS lens. we will read a wide range of authors and viewpoints, and welcome any additions!
what is STS? STS stands for science and technology studies, an interdisciplinary field focused on the metastudy of science, big Science ™️, technology, and the interplay of those elements in society.
a brief glimpse at authors, pieces, and themes we will discuss include: •Neil Postman, Amusing Ourselves to Death •Jean Baudrillard, especially Simulacra and Simulation and •Guy Debord, Society of the Spectacle •Byung Chul-Han and the idea of the neoliberal technological paradigm as one of self-panopticization and self-arresting of agency •Marshall McLuhan, Understanding Media •Walter Benjamin, the Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction •Theodore Adorno, excerpts from Minima Moralia and broader cultural industry critiques •Jacques Ellul’s The Technological Society •Martin Heidegger’s The Question Concerning Technology •Oswald Spengler’s Man and Technics

This is Event Session 1 on November 2nd from 6pm to 9pm
AI changes the game, so what’s next? This is something we ponder as we watch the entire scientific and mathematical universe get shaken up by these new tools we call LLM’s. What it means to program has changed. The trade-offs, the assumptions, the rules that for many years stood for good reason all need a re-think. What things are still true about software engineering and what things change?
What should compilers look like now that humans aren’t maintaining the code? What should code look like? How can we design and equip ourselves for the future with new chip architectures and technologies like spatial fabrics, 3D stacking on chips, photonics and photonic interconnect, statistical computing, and in the future diamond quantum superconducting chips.
How can we engineer a future that spurs innovation and technological progress? This working group meets in person in the Bay Area the first and third Monday of each month to figure out the answers to these questions.
We believe these questions are fundamentally important for the future of humanity, in order to usher in a future of abundance we must spur technological progress and encourage healthy competition in the ecosystem.
Event Session 2 will be held November 16th at 6pm - 9pm on Stanford’s campus.
event.title: The Future Of Compilers And Programming Languages
